version.value: Figaro’s Italian-language entrance aria, recorded as a standalone acoustic disc side
version.note: The label identifies Act I, a baritone and orchestral accompaniment. This is the published aria side, not a complete opera or a recording of the surrounding recitatives. The performing edition, cuts and exact studio orchestration are not established. The listening guide groups broad passages from the historical full score; it does not claim word-level synchronisation.

performers.note: Bolig and Milmo identify Pasternack as conductor. The label states ‘Baritone with orchestra’; neither it nor the consulted discography names the orchestral players.

date.note: All three sources associate matrix C-23945, take 2, with this date. It is not Ruffo’s separate 1912 recording of the same aria.

place.note: Bolig and Milmo list Camden for this matrix. No particular studio room or street address is established.

label.note: The accompanying National Jukebox label image shows a red Victrola label and the Victor Talking Machine Company name.

catalogue.note: The transferred carrier’s label reads 6263-A. The discographies connect the same matrix with both Victor numbers and HMV DB 405; the exact pressing date of the photographed copy is unknown.

matrixTakeSides.value: C-23945, take 2; side A of Victor 6263
matrixTakeSides.note: The matrix and take are identified by the catalogue metadata and discography; the label establishes the side. Stamper and pressing-run details are not established.

credits.value: Library of Congress Packard Campus for Audio Visual Conservation; National Jukebox MP3 mirrored by Hessel Digital Library
credits.note: These are the digitisation and mirror credits stated in the Internet Archive item, which links to the original National Jukebox record. The Library of Congress record identifies its source disc as Victor 6263-A, matrix C-23945-2. No individual transfer engineer is identified.

date.note: The Library of Congress digitisation date is not supplied. The mirror describes a 30 September 2026 retrieval of the LOC MP3; that is a copying event, not the recording or digitisation date.

processing.value: The mirror reports a bit-exact copy of the Library of Congress MP3, with no processing added by the uploader.
processing.note: The uploader states a bit-exact copy. The Library of Congress master WAV of Victor 6263-A has the same duration, 247.78 seconds, and the same performance at the same speed and pitch throughout; byte identity with the Library’s own access MP3 has not been checked. The original stylus, playback speed, equalisation, noise reduction and restoration settings remain unknown.

digital.format: VBR MP3 mirror of a Library of Congress National Jukebox acoustic-disc transfer

composition.value: Rossini’s music and Sterbini’s Italian libretto are out of copyright under ordinary life-plus-70 terms.
composition.note: Rossini died in 1868 and Sterbini in 1831. This assessment covers the historical work, not unidentified modern arrangements or editions.

recording.value: US public domain: first published no later than 1924, on double-faced Victor 6263; the mirror carries the Public Domain Mark.
recording.note: Selected under the project’s us-published-before-cutoff rule. Victor’s 1924 catalogue lists the Ruffo Largo al factotum on 6263, which is absent from the 1923 catalogue; the Library of Congress identifies 6263-A as this matrix. The same recording was also issued on single-faced Victor 88391, replacing Ruffo’s 1912 recording under that number; the mirror states first publication in 1920, but no dated release source was found. On either date, US protection ended no later than 31 December 2024. The Public Domain Mark is a status declaration, not a new licence grant or a worldwide clearance.
